newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank moves against nine ailing banks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank moves against nine ailing banks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday it had placed nine commercial banks under special supervision in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector.

"The central bank decided to place under a special supervisison nine banks in order to restore financial stability through rehabilitation and restructuring of the banking system," the BNB said in a statement after a board meeting.

The banks are Trade and Savings Bank (TSB), Balkanbank, Economic Bank, Businessbank, Elitbank, Slavyani commercial bank, Mollov bank, Yambol commercial bank, and Dobrudzha commercial bank, the statement said.

Placing these banks under special supervision was part of a larger package of measures agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) under a $580 million funding agreement sealed in July, the BNB said.
Supervision, which entails ban on lending, will allow these banks to boost their capital and facilitate their sale to foreign investors.
The BNB said that such negotiations have begun already with the two large state institutions Balkanbank and Economic Bank.

The decision against the nine banks was taken on the eve of IMF/World Bank annual meeting where the Socialist government hopes to win a second $115 million tranche of funding which was previously delayed by the IMF due to Bulgaria's failure to meet reform targets.
Bulgaria pledged to close down loss makers, including banks by end-September.
This was yet another bid by the government to meet funding requirements after opening insolvency procedures through the courts against five other banks in May and June.
